semantic_correction.stem: A pregnant client with placenta accreta spectrum is scheduled for delivery at a center prepared for major obstetric hemorrhage. Which pre-delivery nursing coordination action is most important?

options.A: Confirm blood-bank coordination with the planned delivery so compatible blood products can be mobilized rapidly if needed.
options.B: Wait for active hemorrhage before contacting the blood bank because advance preparation does not change response time.
options.C: Rely on crystalloid availability because placenta accreta spectrum rarely requires large-volume transfusion.
options.D: Stop other hemorrhage planning once blood-bank preparation is complete because it replaces multidisciplinary preparation.

semantic_correction.rationale: ACOG guidance for placenta accreta spectrum recommends delivery planning at appropriately resourced centers with access to a blood bank capable of massive transfusion. It specifically recommends notification and collaboration with the blood bank in concert with delivery and surgical planning because large-volume transfusion is frequently needed and compatibility can be difficult. Blood-bank preparation is one component of a broader multidisciplinary hemorrhage plan and should occur before bleeding begins rather than after an emergency develops.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Coordinate blood-bank readiness before delivery for clients at high risk of major obstetric hemorrhage so blood products can be mobilized rapidly within a multidisciplinary plan.
semantic_correction.source_organization: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG)
semantic_correction.source_document_title: Placenta Accreta Spectrum — Obstetric Care Consensus
semantic_correction.source_locator: Relevant Considerations for Case Optimization — coordination of blood bank with scheduling/timing of case; Management — notification and collaboration with the blood bank is recommended with delivery/surgical planning because large-volume transfusion is frequently required and crossmatching may be difficult; centers should have MTP-capable blood-bank access
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: For placenta accreta spectrum, advance notification and collaboration with the blood bank should be integrated into delivery planning because severe hemorrhage and large-volume transfusion may occur.
semantic_correction.blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)

semantic_correction.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — blood-bank preparedness for anticipated obstetric hemorrhage
semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: shortened the uniquely long correct answer, kept the nursing action at the coordination level, and anchored the item to ACOG's explicit pre-delivery blood-bank notification/collaboration recommendation.

audit_findings_append.source_locator: Placenta Accreta Spectrum — blood-bank coordination and delivery planning
audit_findings_append.finding: The original answer was uniquely longest. The revised item directly tests advance blood-bank coordination as one component of multidisciplinary hemorrhage readiness.

option_audit.A: Correct. It directly matches ACOG's recommendation to coordinate blood-bank readiness with planned delivery and surgery.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Waiting for active hemorrhage creates avoidable delay in a condition with substantial transfusion risk.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Placenta accreta spectrum can cause life-threatening hemorrhage and frequently requires transfusion.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Blood-bank readiness supplements rather than replaces multidisciplinary hemorrhage planning.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone performs the source-supported pre-delivery coordination action without delaying or replacing the broader care plan.
cueing_check: All four choices are pre-delivery planning statements of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
